### 3. Calculate & record recent virus titer experiment

Based on the previous p24 standard curve, the following values were determined for the new batch of viruses with the amounts required for infection at MOI=200.

![](assets/img/doc3-image2.png)

Based on these values, it was also observed that Gcla, GCD-1 were packaged and concentrated at 4 degrees for \~40-48 hours, while GCD-2, HCD were concentrated for only \~20-24 hours. Quite a significant difference in the titer is seen in these cases.

### 4. Set up reconstitution for lig20K, lig50K with recombinant human histone octamer

*lig20K*

Use 3.89 ug of DNA

lig20K (D6) ⇒ 15 uL ⇒ 15 nM \[at 2 M salt concentration\]

Octamer stock ⇒ 1.07 ug/uL

Octamer molarity acc. to 60:1 ratio ⇒ 0.9 uM ⇒ 1.96 ug in 5 uL ⇒ Prepare 500 ng/uL stock OH500 (3.74 uL \+ 4.26 uL refolding buffer) ⇒ 3.92 uL OH500 \+ 1.08 uL refolding buffer \+ glycerol} 

### 5. Set up reconstitution for GP5d-20K with WT histone octamer (D5 repeat)

*GP5d-20K \[x1\]*

Use 3.89 ug of DNA \[				\]

*GP5d-20K* (D5) ⇒ 15 uL ⇒ 15 nM \[at 2 M salt concentration\]

Prepare 5 uL octamer stock \[3.92 uL O500 \+ 1.08 uL refolding buffer \+ glycerol\] \[1.78 M\] ⇒ Final concentration of mix \[1.95 M\]

This trial is being run at 1.5 mL/min (pump 1\) & 1.3 mL/min (pump 2\)

### 7. lig147 ligand plate preparation

Concentration of original lig147 ssDNA tube is about 4.8 ug/uL

Dilute this 1:200 ⇒ 1 uL oligo \+ 199 uL TE buffer (lig147-dil200)

PCR 1 → 100X

| Reagent | Volume (µL) |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Final diluted DNA** | **20** |
| **Phusion Master Mix** | **525** |
| **NCAP\_F (10 µM)** | **52.5** |
| **NCAP\_R (10 uM)** | **52.5** |
| **Water** | **400**  |
| **Total** | **1,050** |

This uses \~10-12 ng of the ssDNA as template per reaction.

 

| 98°C | 3 min |
| :---- | :---- |
| 98°C | 10 s |
| 55°C | 15 s       **8X\*** |
| 72°C | 30 s |
| 72°C | 40 min |
| 4°C | HOLD |

Pool all PCR products and run 20 uL on an agarose gel to check the purity of the product. Once confirmed that the product is of good quality, pool all reactions together and purify the product to final pure ligand (of each type).

The band from PCR 1 was very clean and the yield was seen to be \~28 ng/uL.

For one 384-well plate with \~25 uL of 20 ng/uL DNA per well ⇒ Total yield needed is 200 ug ⇒ If we set up PCR on a 96-well plate, this scales down to about 2 ug yield per well

Prepare a 1000 uL solution of DNA with 710 uL of PCR1 (+290 uL TE buffer) ⇒ 20 ng/uL DNA mix ⇒ Add 10 uL per well

| Reagent | Volume (µL) |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Final diluted DNA** | **1000** |
| **Phusion Master Mix** | **2500** |
| **NCAP\_F (10 µM)** | **250** |
| **NCAP\_R (10 uM)** | **250** |
| **Water** | **1000**  |
| **Total** | **5000** |

| 98°C | 3 min |
| :---- | :---- |
| 98°C | 10 s |
| 55°C | 15 s       **3X\*** |
| 72°C | 30 s |
| 72°C | 40 min |
| 4°C | HOLD |

Pool all PCR products and run 20 uL on an agarose gel to check the purity of the product. Once confirmed that the product is of good quality, pool all reactions together and purify the product to final pure ligand (of each type).

### 8. D4, D5 recon lower salt dialysis

500 mL

| 1 M Tris pH 8 | 7.5 mL |
| :---- | :---- |
| EDTA (0.5 M) | 1 mL |
| EGTA (0.5 M) | 500 uL |
| KCl (4 M) | 10 mL |
| TCEP | 5 mL |
| Glycerol | 25 mL |

Allow this buffer to mix and then use vacuum to purify the buffer. Store buffer.

Take 3 mini-dialysis columns labeled D4, D4 and D5 and then place them on top of the buffer solution for equilibration.

After equilibration, transfer the original reconstituted samples in D1, D2, D3 to each of the new mini dialysis columns. During the transfer, rinse the original columns with a little of the Buffer C and add this to the transferred samples undergoing buffer exchange. Leave this system O/N at 4 degrees.
